interval.d: A stretch of inputs between two ends, such as the times from 1 s to 3 s. An average rate is always taken over an interval.

power rule.d: The derivative of tⁿ is n·tⁿ⁻¹. For example t² has derivative 2t and t³ has derivative 3t². It comes from expanding (t + Δt)ⁿ and keeping only the term with one Δt.

forward difference.d: A numerical derivative that looks one step ahead: (f(x + Δx) − f(x)) / Δx. Its error shrinks in proportion to the step Δx, until rounding error takes over for very small steps.

double precision.d: The usual way a computer stores a real number: 64 bits, about 16 significant decimal digits. Subtracting two numbers that agree in most of those digits leaves mostly rounding noise.
